idiom_name: zod schema as the executable contract (types via z.infer), or types generated from OpenAPI/JSON Schema plus a runtime validator
implementation_notes: TypeScript types vanish at runtime, so the published language has to be an executable artifact: either a zod schema whose z.infer type keeps code and contract in one declaration (zod can emit the JSON Schema for the document), or types generated from the schema document (openapi-typescript) combined with a runtime validator such as Ajv for the payloads the compiler cannot check. Generation must run in CI so the committed types cannot drift from the published schema. The hand-written interface plus casts form stays acceptable only for payloads that never cross a published boundary.
pitfalls: A type annotation is not a check: `const o: Order = JSON.parse(body)` compiles and lies - only a runtime parse (zod/Ajv) or generated validator enforces the published schema.
Generated types drift when the generator runs by hand; wire it into CI and fail the build when the committed artifacts differ from the schema.
zod strips unknown keys by default and offers .passthrough()/.strict(): the choice is part of the tolerance policy, and strip silently discards data a forwarder might need to preserve.
